Exchange-Students-Programm der Technischen Hochschule Augsburg
Exchange Students
You would like to spend one or two semesters as an exchange student in Germany? Then pack your bags and come to the Technical University of Applied Sciences Augsburg (THA)! As an exchange student, you’ll study at THA, gain new perspectives, and explore Augsburg. On this page, you’ll find all the important information you need for your stay, from applying to arriving.
Important Infos at a Glance
Study for 1–2 exchange semesters at THA.
Join us as a student from one of our international partner universities or as a freemover.
Choose from a wide range of courses from various academic fields.
Take courses taught in German and English.
Gain international study experience and earn ECTS toward your degree at home.
Get to know Augsburg, Bavaria, and Germany.
Make connections with students from all over the world.
Nomination deadlines for partner universities: April 30 (winter semester) and October 31 (summer semester)
Application deadlines for students: May 15 (winter semester) and November 15 (summer semester)

What exactly is a student exchange program?
Our exchange program allows you to study at THA for 1–2 semesters. As an exchange student, you’ll come to Augsburg from abroad and enroll in regular courses here, either in German or English. For the duration of the exchange, you’ll be enrolled at both your home university and the THA, and you can generally use the ECTS earned at the THA for your degree program back home. This way, you’ll gain international experience, meet new people, and experience Germany firsthand.
Here's what your time at THA will look like
Your time at THA begins with the
Welcome and Orientation Week
. For the winter semester, you’ll arrive in Augsburg between September 15 and 30; for the summer semester, between March 1 and 14. During this time, you’ll get to know the university, your campus, and your faculty. You’ll receive important information to help you get started with your studies, set up your THA user account, and take care of some initial administrative tasks. You’ll also get to know Augsburg right away: a guided city tour will give you a first impression of your new home. You can also take part in a German Survival Crash Course and start making connections with other international students.
After that, your
exchange semester
will really get underway. The winter semester runs from October 1 to March 14, and the summer semester from March 15 to September 30. You’ll attend the courses you’ve chosen, earn ECTS, and study alongside students from Germany and around the world. Of course, there will still be time outside of your studies to explore Augsburg and the surrounding region. The city combines over 2,000 years of history with a vibrant student life, culture, sports, and plenty of nature. Whether it’s cafés, concerts, university sports, festivals, swimming lakes, or day trips to the surrounding area—you won’t get bored here anytime soon.
At the end of your stay, it’s time for your exams. In the winter semester, the
exam period
usually runs from January 15 to February 14. In the summer semester, you’ll typically take your exams from July 15 to July 31.
During your stay, you’ll be part of an international community. You’ll meet people from many different countries, take part in events and activities, and can make Augsburg your home away from home. And eventually, it’s time to say goodbye. Then you’ll head back home, with many new experiences, international connections, and hopefully plenty of great memories to take with you.
Which courses do you want to pick?
For your exchange semester, you’ll put together your
Learning Agreement
(see section 3 in
“How to apply for your exchange”
) from the courses offered. We recommend taking
15 to 30 ECTS
per semester.
You can usually find the courses offered by your faculty on their website. An overview of most courses offered in English is available
here
. It’s possible that not all courses listed on our website will be offered during your exchange semester. Therefore, check with your faculty or your International Faculty Coordinator (IFC) if you’re unsure.
In general, you can also choose courses from other departments. However, they should be relevant to your degree program at your home university. Final admission is granted by the respective faculty or IFC. Please also note that certain courses require specific prerequisites.
Not sure which courses are right for you? Then contact your faculty’s IFC. He or she will be happy to help you choose your courses. You can also adjust your Learning Agreement during Welcome and Orientation Week if needed. Since the detailed semester schedule won’t be finalized until later, the courses you can choose may still change before the semester begins.
How to apply for your exchange
Would you like to study at THA for one or two semesters? Here are the six steps to join us:
1. Your home university nominates you
Before you apply to us, your home university must nominate you for an exchange semester at THA.
2. You apply online
After you are nominated, you will receive the information you need to apply. Fill out the
online application form
(for EPS, use
this form
) on Mobility-Online.
3. Upload your documents
These include, among other things:
a
passport or ID photo
(no stamps or markings; max. 500x500 pixels)
the
Learning Agreement
(EU students should use the Erasmus+ form from their home university; non-EU students should use this
form
)
a
resume
in German or English (including your proficiency level in German and English)
a
transcript of records
from your home university showing your academic performance prior to your stay
a
copy of your passport or ID card
(both sides) and
residence permit
(if required)
proof of your health insurance
Depending on your degree program or country of origin, additional documents may be required. Students from the Faculty of Design and the Faculty of Architecture and Civil Engineering should also attach a portfolio or include a link to it in their resume.
Please note the following regarding
health
insurance
: European students need the European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). Non-European students must obtain German health insurance upon arrival. If you are an EU student and do not have a valid EHIC, please upload a signed letter containing the following statement: “I hereby declare that I do not have a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). I confirm that I will apply for valid German health insurance upon my arrival.”
4. Submit your application
Upload all required documents in their entirety to Mobility-Online and submit your application. The application deadline is May 15 for the winter semester and November 15 for the summer semester.
5. You'll receive your acceptance letter
The THA will review your application. If everything checks out, you'll receive confirmation that you've been accepted for your exchange semester.
6. You'll make arrangements for your trip
Once you’ve been accepted, you’ll need to arrange your travel and everything else you’ll need for your stay. Depending on your country of origin, this may include, for example, a visa, health insurance, and housing. Make sure to find out what you need well in advance so you can start your exchange semester feeling relaxed.
And then it’s time to say: Welcome to Augsburg! Participation in the Welcome and Orientation Week is mandatory. There, you’ll get to know the THA, receive important information to help you get started, and meet other international students.
When do the semesters at THA start, and what are the application deadlines?
The
winter semester
at THA runs from October 1 to March 14. Your home university must nominate you for the winter semester by April 30. You must upload your application materials to Mobility-Online by May 15.
The
summer semester
runs from March 15 to September 30. The nomination must be submitted by October 31. You must upload your application documents by November 15.
Plan ahead and keep an eye on the deadlines. Then nothing will stand in the way of your stay!
How can I finance my stay abroad?
There are various options for financing your exchange semester. It’s best to research scholarships and funding programs before you arrive. A good place to start is the
DAAD’s scholarship database
, which offers numerous funding opportunities for international students.
In general, you may also take on part-time work during your stay in Germany. Please note, however, that different regulations apply depending on your nationality and visa status. Therefore, be sure to find out well in advance which regulations apply to you.
What do I need to know about visas?
Whether you need a visa for your exchange semester at THA depends on your nationality. Are you studying at a partner university outside of Europe and do not hold European citizenship? If so, you must apply for your visa well in advance at the German embassy or consulate in your home country. Find out about the requirements well in advance and submit your application as soon as possible. Processing can take several weeks or even months.
You can find more information about visas on our
visa page
. If you have any questions, please contact the
Academic Immigration Office
.
What do I need to consider when it comes to housing?
Finding a place to live in Augsburg can take some time. That’s why we recommend that you start your search early. The THA does not have its own dormitories, but we’re happy to help you find suitable housing. You’ll find all the important information and helpful tips on our
page about housing
.
I have some questions before or during my stay. Who can I contact?
Whether before you arrive or during your exchange semester, we’re here for you. If you have any questions about the application process, your studies, or your stay, the exchange program coordinator,
Katharina Leuthmetzer
, will be happy to help.
Would you like some first-hand tips or to meet someone who knows their way around THA? Then get in touch with your
Buddy
from our
SWOP team
. Our Buddies will help you settle in, explore Augsburg with you, and help you quickly find your feet at THA.
My stay is coming to an end. What do I need to do?
Before you head home, there are a few organizational matters to take care of.
Deregister your current address at the city office.
If necessary, close your German bank account and cancel your insurance policies.
Check to make sure all your exam results are entered in HIS Online.
Once all your grades are available, you can download your official Transcript of Records.
You can find a detailed checklist and all further information on our
page about the end of your stay
.
Best of luck with your future endeavors, and hopefully we’ll see you again soon in Augsburg!
